headline: IndustrialVLA-Bench separates clean simulation scores from robustness and instruction sensitivity
summary: An October 2026 preprint evaluates six released vision-language-action and world-action robot policies across clean LIBERO tasks, visual/embodiment perturbations, instruction paraphrases and observed runtime costs. Across the six systems, the paper reports only a 1.58-point spread on clean LIBERO but larger spreads on visual robustness and paraphrase success. Three systems are marked protocol-faithful; near-reproduction and pending-verification rows remain diagnostic and are excluded from strict comparisons. Results are limited to selected checkpoints in LIBERO-family simulation, not real-robot performance or causal architectural comparisons.
